item.title: Sigsheet: one file for signing CKB multisig transactions across ckb-cli, Neuron and CCC apps (first spec draft, feedback wanted) (1 posts)
item.description: Hi everyone, We’ve published the first draft of Sigsheet, an open file format for signing a CKB multisig transaction. Each signer uses the wallet they already have: ckb-cli, Neuron, or an app built on CCC. We’d like your feedback before we write the implementations. The problem A CKB multisig transaction is usually signed by several people, often with different tools. Today two things get in the way. Partial signatures don’t travel between tools. ckb-cli, Neuron, CCC and ckb-sdk each hold a partly signed multisig transaction in a different way. The incompatibility between ckb-cli’s tx file and Neuron was reported in 2024 (ckb-cli#584, neuron#3048). In our tests with ckb-cli 2.0.0, Neuron...

item.description: Funding requested: $1,000 Project duration: 6 weeks Category: Developer Tools / Privacy Target ecosystem: Nervos CKB License: Open source Applicant: Owais (GitHub: owaisdotcom) · Full Stack Software Engineer 1. Project Overview Unlinked for CKB is an open-source browser extension prototype designed to improve privacy when interacting with Nervos CKB decentralized applications. It adapts the anon-rpc architecture and browser-based Tor client (tor-js, based on Arti compiled to WebAssembly) to the CKB ecosystem. item.title: DAO提案公平性疑问？ (4 posts)
item.description: Rosen项目是社区DAO很好的一次教训，当时不少社区成员都猜到了结局，最终却还是没能拦住，它也伤害了社区的元气： [DIS] CKB Integration for Rosen Bridge 随着这个桥的完成，当我们发现，桥建好了，什么都没有发生，没有什么有益的事情在ckb上面因为rosen bridge这个桥的建立而产生，唯一真实发生的就是，ckb的dao资金真实划拨给了那几位开发者，那么投赞成票里面哪一位应该对此负责？ [DIS] CKB Integration for Rosen Bridge 我感受到一种害怕，多数立场者，利益是一致的，他们的投票可以很容易的决定投票的走向，比如对于这个提案，我恶意的猜测，国外友人他们都是认识的，并且熟悉的，他们不需要对于这个提案的失败负责，毕竟大家是一起投票的 [DIS] CKB Integration for Rosen Bridge 如果这样的提案能够通过，我觉得我对ckb不会再抱有任何期待，我实在想不通连接了两个完全没有人的社区的一个桥梁，这个桥梁的建设能够值这么多ckb，“这真是一笔好生意”，也许应该建造，但绝对不是现在，如果通过后，我会抛售我持有的所有ckb，并且退出所有关于ckb的相关频道。 它曾是当时争议最大的DAO提案之一。尽管遭遇了大量社区成员的明确反对，但它仍靠着熟人圈子和部分元老的站台强行过关。结果呢？一些人失望而走，项目最终烂尾，DAO也白白损失了宝贵的国库资金，这是一个三败俱伤的教训。 不希望看到这种类似熟人互助/利益交换的剧本在现在的DAO项目中重演，你们觉得呢？ @phroi @matt_ckb...

item.description: 1. Project Overview Project name: MoniMkt One-line summary: A reusable CKB lending validation toolkit, field-tested with real users against the MoniMkt testnet product. item.title: [DIS] KeyMe — CKB's PSBT: Open Air-Gapped Signing and the First DIY Hardware (3 posts)
item.description: Pretty cool. Glad to see a new approach to open transaction signing and standardization. Thanks for the kind words, and for reading the Reflections series. You’re right that Neuron supports offline signing, including offline multisig; it’s an important precedent. v1 stays focused on the hardware and PSCT; v2 will explore potential pathways with Neuron. Appreciate the support. Thanks, glad it resonates. The standardization is the part I care about most: PSCT is deliberately an open container, not a wallet-specific format, so independent tools can build, inspect and sign the same transaction. Appreciate the kind words.

item.title: Spark Program | Lifeboat: see what an address owns on CKB, and get it out when the app is gone (1 posts)
item.description: A second question I expect, about safety: should a third-party tool be building exit transactions for other people’s assets at all? For a product that is gone, there is nobody else left to do it. The original team has stopped, so the real choice is between a public, reviewable tool and each holder piecing together raw transactions alone. Lifeboat is built to keep that risk small: It never holds keys or funds. The holder signs in their own wallet. Every transaction is shown in full before signing, and each output is checked against the locks the connected wallet controls, so anything going to an address that is not theirs is flagged. item.title: C-KZG-4844 on CKB-VM & Blob tree (1 posts)
item.description: Port c-kzg-4844 to CKB-VM; see EIP-4844 for more details. We also introduce a blob tree built on c-kzg-4844. We already have SMT, but SMT proofs are quite large, especially when proving multiple elements at once. So we propose a new solution: the blob tree. At its core, it is a two-level path tree built on c-kzg-4844 with Shplonk. It commits to as many as 16,777,216 (4096×4096) elements in a tree of just two levels. Whether you query one element or many, the proof reduces to a single KZG verification call. github.com GitHub - XuJiandong/c-kzg-4844: A minimal implementation of the Polynomial... port-riscv A minimal implementation of the Polynomial Commitments API for EIP-4844 and EIP-7594,...
